To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we propose a novel Cloud-based system that provides fast and customized driving routes for a user, (ii) we design and implement an effective model to predict the travel time of the route for a user, and (iii) we evaluate the system using a real-world data set of over 33, 000 taxis over a 3-month period.
(i) our system can accurately predict travel time and find the fastest route for a user, and (ii) our system can learn the user's driving behavior and adapt to the user's preference.
our system can compute a fast and customized driving route for an end user based on historical and real-time traffic conditions and the user's driving behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How to build a model that incorporates the physical and virtual worlds and predicts future traffic conditions? How to build a Cloud-based service that can compute the fastest route for a user?

the following questions: How can we use the knowledge of the physical world to improve the driving route computation? How can we make a driving route service self-adaptive to a driver's individual driving behavior?
the following questions: How to build a system that can compute customized and practically fast routes for an end-user? How to make the route computing service adaptive to a particular user?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our system provides an accurate, fast, and customized driving route service for an end user.
our system is the first Cloud-based driving route service using both historical and real-time traffic information and driver intelligence.

this paper proposes an intelligent and efficient Cloud-based service to compute a fast driving route for a particular user, and it demonstrates the feasibility of such a service using a large-scale real-world dataset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our system is a novel and practically useful service to end users, and it is also an interesting application for Cloud computing.
our system can be used as a Cloud-based driving direction service that provides a customized and practically fast route for a particular user, which is a significant step toward a smart city.
we present a Cloud-based system to compute the fastest route for a user using the knowledge from the physical (taxi) world and the Cloud, and the user's driving behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cloud can be a useful platform for integrating the physical world with the virtual world, and for providing a customized service for a user.
we demonstrate that it is possible to build a Cloud-based system to predict the traffic conditions in a city and to find the fastest driving route for a particular user.
a Cloud-based service can learn from the physical world to improve the service quality of the Cloud.
